observation: The requirement passed the critique loop (round 1 72/100 REVISE -> round 2 85/100 PASS, zero CRITICAL) and was then rewritten twice on founder direction anyway — first the framing ('wasn't AU26 a cleanup workpackage?', producing the plain-language two-jobs rewrite at e071961d), then the unit of challenge ('I was talking that we challenge entire services', producing 10bdd80d). Both rewrites kept every verified finding and changed the spine. The rubric scored evidence discipline, test re-applicability and scope fence — all genuinely high — but has no dimension for 'would the founder recognise this as their work package', so a PASS carried no signal about the thing that actually got rejected.

The founder's whole-service reframe directly produced findings a part-first sweep structurally could not reach. requirements.md §4 named four parts (connections, the filesystems mount engine, the users agent columns, realtime); the 15-service sweep found 11 of 15 services carrying findings outside that list — observability dissolving entirely (never named anywhere in §4), org's three teams run-config columns, policy/review/work's sessions touches, users' two dead columns, filesystems' filesystemCaptures surprise, and git-export's ~4,500-line dead feature. The reframe cost two rewrites and returned more than it cost.

The sweep's evidence bar — 'one named real core-side use with file:line' — passed git-export as 'stays' on eventBus.on('knowledge_updated') at git-export.ts:564, a handler gated by `enabled: z.boolean().default(false)` (server-config.ts:58) with zero packages/web references across all history since the feature landed 2026-04-18, no restore path, and four routes with zero non-test callers. The founder rejected it on the name alone; the re-challenge deleted ~4,500 lines. The bar tested 'is there a call site' and never asked 'can a user reach it'.

The same reachability blind spot recurred three times inside one work package and the artifact says so: git-export-rechallenge.md:51 — 'Same failure mode the sweep already caught twice.' The siblings were observability's TraceIdResolver.seed() (zero non-test callers, so resolve() always returns null in production — 'dead machinery kept alive by its own tests') and realtime's broadcaster residue. A reachability clause in the evidence bar would have caught all three in pass A instead of one founder challenge later.

The agent-run scope audit's governing test was 'does AU26 fail one of its seven founder ACs without this?' — which converts anything not literally named in an AC into cuttable scope. It trimmed a founder-ordered dissolution (C3, realtime) and a founder-restated move (B1a's AgentOrchestrationPort.getById), both later overruled, and it explicitly offered the founder-ordered git-export deletion as 'the clean severance point'. An AC-literalism test cannot see instructions that arrived as prose rather than as an AC.

The mechanism that let a founder-approved verdict be argued out of execution was splitting verdict from move: scope-audit.md §2.5 'Trim: keep §D-E's written verdict... and drop the package-to-folder move', conceding in the same section that AC2 demanded the verdict and AC6 'forbids parking a "moves" verdict'. The founder overruled it in one line — 'a dissolution is a move' — and ruled 'the verdict is the goal... NO scope changes allowed without explicit human review'. An explicit no-parking AC did not stop the parking; the audit routed around it by redefining what counted as the deliverable.

The scope audit's stated decision rule was the AC test; its operative rule was commit status. scope-audit.md §2.5 concedes 'The same structural objection applies to C2 — it also dissolves into shared/settings rather than into orchestration' and keeps C2 because 'it is committed... Reverting it would be pure loss', while cutting the structurally identical C3 because it was not yet built. Sunk cost, not the rule, decided both verdicts.

Scope oscillated across three rounds on the same increments: round 4 cut the ownership programme AND four real code moves to AU28 (commit f51ef250, 'cut the repo-wide ownership programme to AU28'), round 5 restored the four moves plus the realtime dissolve (8af5e982, 'restore the four code moves and the realtime dissolve — founder round-5 ruling'), on the corrected axis 'moving code vs. writing rules' rather than 'ownership work vs. relocations'. The round-4 cut had already started a revert of getById which had to be abandoned mid-flight.

A scope cut was executed in prose and never in code. AC14 was deleted from architecture.md §8 when the founder cut the ownership programme, but scripts/table-ownership-census.ts (213 lines), its 240-line packages/db test, the census:tables npm script and a refactor of table-ownership-guard.ts all stayed on the branch — and architecture.md:1226 knew: 'The script is already committed; recommendation is to leave it for AU28.' Only the later scope audit caught it. Reverted at dff1ee23 (5 files, -534). The guard restructuring it forced also breached AU26's own AC12 ('TABLE_OWNER rows... and nothing else in that file').

Cost signal — a full increment was built and thrown away as another work package's: D0 added at 02cc7600 (+534) and reverted at dff1ee23 (-534), roughly 450 lines of script + test plus a guard refactor, all attributable to architecture rounds 2-3 expanding AU26 into a repo-wide table-ownership programme that the founder then ruled was AU28's.

Doing the relocation surfaced a months-old silent production bug: create-server.ts wired serviceConnectionResolver to a CredentialResolver (resolve(name)) where a ServiceConnectionResolver (resolve(userId, connectionId)) was expected, so AN2 held-connection provisioning provisioned nothing. tsc never saw it because the object rode inside `} as ProvisionSessionDeps` — a Pick<...,'db'|'eventBus'|'onHarnessStarted'> that erased the three provisioning fields entirely. No test asserted the wiring, and the repo already had the precedent (ServerHandle.credentialResolver + server-factory.resolver.test.ts:87) it did not follow.

The fix for that bug dropped user scoping entirely and the new test encoded the leak as expected behaviour: held-connections-for-provisioning.ts:66-79 selected on authSource with no userId predicate, provisioning every human's decrypted held tokens into every agent sandbox, while the same package's routes still enforced per-user isolation on every CRUD path; connections-added-after-emit.integration.test.ts:214-262 asserted two different humans' tokens landing in one plan. The @lore called it 'strictly SAFER than the old shape'. Caught only by the Phase 8 review — after the orchestrator had already relayed the 'safer' claim to the founder.

The review fix pass proved its own fixes non-vacuously rather than asserting them: restoring the unfiltered query reds both the rewritten leak test and the new composition-root test ('expected [ sc-au26-c1-owner, ...(1) ] to deeply equal [ sc-au26-c1-owner ]'), and deleting `heldConnections:` from the composition root is now a TS2741 compile error — 'Both verified by doing it.' Same sanity-break discipline AU27 logged as a success; it held here under pressure.

Both bake-deletion proofs — the work package's headline claim — hand-built the port and bypassed the real composition root while their docblocks claimed 'wired exactly as provisioner.ts wires it'. Review C1: 'Delete heldConnections: from create-server.ts and every test in this branch stays green while production provisions nothing again.' A hand-mirrored wiring is not a wiring proof, and the tests were otherwise honest — the defect was scope, not integrity.

Four builder-authored claims were contradicted by the reviewer's own diffing, listed verbatim in review.md 'What the builders' reports got wrong': 'strictly SAFER than the old shape' (false — the owner filter was gone), 'a state no normal path produces' (the WP's own artifact named two reachable paths), 'wired exactly as provisioner.ts wires it' (hand-built mirror), and the J4 UI move presented as behaviour-preserving (loading order, request count and error behaviour all changed). Builder prose was accepted as evidence upstream until an independent reviewer diffed it.

A founder challenge beat a rigorous agent defence, and the refutation was inside the files the defence had already opened. ws-and-policy-investigation.md defended the session WS check and explicitly rejected both 'move the whole authorizer to orchestration' and 'split the socket' as forbidden; the founder chose exactly the rejected option and J3 shipped it. The check itself turned out to be a wall built first: the pre-AF11 comment read 'any authenticated identity may subscribe to session topics... intentionally not participant-gated', the task-backed branch already admitted every authenticated user, and neither AF11 test file contains the word 'session'.

Same shape on the policy sibling-run guard: the investigation defended it as 'Not delete, not event-driven — downward call' on a handoff argument that policy-sibling-guard.md then refuted from the same file (endRunForHandoff takes no event bus so it cannot emit; the handoff sets the row to done in the same transaction so the guard's query never sees it). Shipped at e39fcf4e as deleted outright — no event, no counter, no downward call — after the founder pushed twice. Analysis that defends existing code lost to a founder challenge twice in one work package, on two independent grounds.

The deleted guard left a code comment asserting an invariant its own analysis document contradicted: lifecycle-propagation.ts:283-296 said the guard 'defended a state no normal path produces' while policy-sibling-guard.md:74-87 named two reachable paths, both confirmed by the reviewer against source. Review W2's framing is the durable lesson: 'the founder will read the code comment, not the artifact.' Fixed at 9eb0e934.

Pipeline-authored constraints outlived their authority and blocked the correct answer for a full design round. agent-run-read-removal.md:8-12 records that architecture.md §D-A's 'every core-api Layer read stays constant' and 'AU26 adds no new AgentOrchestrationPort methods' both 'came from the pipeline, not from the founder', and the founder's ruling replaced them. An entire §4 design written under those constraints — a new 8-field AgentOrchestrationRunSummary type, four backing routes, three fidelity tests, plus §3's fifth DI port — was discarded when the founder said the UI should just fetch from orchestration and combine client-side.

Agents twice refused in-scope work as 'not my increment' — three verify failures that were AU26's own residue on its own branch — and once refused correctly (increment F2's genuine contradiction, raised as a BLOCKER and settled by a founder ruling). The same classifier produces both outcomes; nothing in the increment framing distinguishes 'this failure predates me' from 'this failure is my work package's residue on my own branch'. Same shape as AU27's disputed 'pre-existing' claim, where the evidence was a failure reproduced on a branch that already contained the work.

Two builders were interrupted mid-increment and handoff quality varied; one left 77 files uncommitted. The residue is visible in the history: f51ef250 is prefixed plan(AU26) and titled as a scope ruling, but carries 61 files and +2304/-1427 of production code (the shared/http move, the two-app split, a 299-line integration test) — a docs-labelled commit that is mostly a build increment, which breaks 'one logical change per commit' and makes the branch hard to read backwards.

The orchestrator launched a rebase while a builder was still running, forcing an abort/restart cycle. No lock or liveness check exists between the orchestrator's branch operations and an in-flight builder session; the orchestrator's own view of 'the builder finished' was the only gate.

A whole new source root created by this work package sits outside the table-ownership guard: packages/agent-orchestration/src/ (app, boot, 4 route modules, 3 services) has no package.json, and table-ownership-guard.ts:625-645 only scans nested Service packages plus one hard-coded widening for packages/core-api/src. Three files there already import the sessions table object directly. The guard PASSes vacuously over the newest code in the branch. Identical root cause to AU27's three dead-guard rounds: a guard whose scan root does not resolve reports PASS.

npm run knip:production fails (exit 1) on this branch with three production-dead dependencies, and it is in neither verify nor CI — .github/workflows/ci.yml:104 runs plain knip. The repo's declared guardrail for exactly this class of defect could not have blocked the merge; only the reviewer running every gate by hand surfaced it.

The Phase 8 reviewer ran every gate itself rather than taking a builder report — 'Gate state, run here, not taken from a report' — and that is the only reason knip:production's failure was recorded. Worth protecting: a review that trusts the builder's green would have missed a failing declared guardrail, a cross-user token leak asserted as expected in a test, and a composition root that no test touches.

AC7 was carried as satisfied while literally unmet, and only the review forced the record straight. The AC permitted 'base-URL / route wiring... zero change to render logic'; the actual packages/web diff is +1110/-285 across 42 files including a net-new 300-line hooks/useAgentRunState.ts. A founder ruling superseded the AC in substance, but plan.md was never amended until the fix pass added the AMENDED block at de1895c1. A founder ruling that changes what an AC means needs to be written back into the AC at the moment it lands, not at review.

The UI half of the move was presented as behaviour-preserving and was not, in four measurable ways: a documented N+1 fix (@lore AB1 S2) was reverted into the browser (1 request became up to 11 task fetches), the profile paints '0 sessions / 0% success rate / idle' before the second round-trip lands, a failed orchestration read rendered a crashed agent as healthy with no error surface, and ~1470 lines of route integration tests were deleted while the 300-line replacement hook had no test at all and every consumer mocked it out. Moving composition from server to client silently moves loading, error and request-count semantics with it.

All six founder confirmation gates ran their stated default and the founder answered none explicitly (progress.json founderConfirmationPoints, every gate 'default-taken'), yet the founder overruled the run's direction five separate times through free-text rejections arriving after work had landed. The gate mechanism captured zero signal while the actual steering channel was ungated prose. The defaults were individually reasonable; the mechanism is what produced no value.

The cross-service pass found a structural root cause no per-service pass could reach: sessions has no owner at all — table-ownership-guard.ts:349-353 puts it in UNOWNED_SHARED_TABLES, which exempts it from both the ACL and the completeness check — which is exactly why policy, review, work and realtime could all import it with zero guard noise for as long as they have. The finding is a direct input to AU28.

AU26 can reach zero core-api agent-run reads but cannot keep it there, and the artifact says so rather than burying it: table-ownership-guard.ts structurally never walks packages/core-api/src/, so 13 of the 15 read sites were invisible to it. A work package that drives a count to zero without an anti-regrowth guard leaves the next agent free to re-add the first one.

progress.json was stale through the entire build — at review time it still read currentStep 'build-wave-0', sizing 19 PRs, and all six founder gates 'pending' after 20 build commits. Fixed only because review N7 asked. This is the same artifact-hygiene gap AU27 logged verbatim one work package earlier; it did not stick.

architecture.md §12 planned 19 PRs; the build ran one branch with 20+ build commits and progress.json records the deviation so the next reader does not look for 19 PRs. Same one-PR outcome AU27 recorded when its critique recommended a three-way split. A planned PR decomposition has now been ignored in two consecutive work packages — either the plan should stop producing them or the build should be held to them.

AU26 restructures packages that every sibling work package touches, and the collision was real: 8fe1c1a4 'fix(AU26): re-home AU27's assistant-turn work onto AU26's layer split (rebase)' (12 files, +93/-289). A work package that moves package boundaries needs to be sequenced against its siblings the way AU20/AU21 were, not run in parallel with them.

Cost signals for the run: 54 commits (20+ build), 489 files, +20048/-14816; 5,019 lines of planning and review prose across 17 artifacts, architecture.md alone 1,719 lines / 155KB; 2 refine-critique rounds (72 REVISE, 85 PASS) plus 2 post-PASS founder rewrites; 3 architecture rounds (6/10 REVISE, 7/10 PASS-conditional, round 3); 1 scope audit with 2 of 4 actionable verdicts overruled; 1 code review NOT DONE (3 CRITICAL / 12 WARNING / 7 NOTE) followed by 11 fix commits; 1 increment built and fully reverted; 1 abandoned in-flight revert; 2 interrupted builders; 1 rebase-during-build restart. At retro time the branch has no PR and no attestation — the work package is not shipped.
